title: Pizza For The House With No DOOR 🍕
premise: Every night at six I bring one large plain pizza to a lemon house with no door and no path, and slide it through a brass slot at knee height. A twenty slides back out, folded into a tiny house. My big sister gave me her route this month, and tonight my tire went flat two blocks away.
twist: The house is somebody enormous sitting very still with a roof on. The slot is its mouth, the top windows its eyes, and one plain pizza a night is what keeps it sitting. Late, it stands and turns toward the nearest lit door; the order only ever says the house with no door, so I deliver it to the bare dirt.
world: a short sundown street of painted houses with porch lights, one doorless lemon-brick house with a brass slot at knee height, and a red-and-white pizza place on the corner

so I ran it

went dark
and lit again
like it blinked

the lawn splits
the house rises, the sky pink behind it
the whole house, standing, roof on
the cover frame: me tiny at its feet
its knees came up
the slot was its mouth; the tally on the flap
every porch light was out
so it turned
toward the one door still lit
Marisol's door

I set it down

of the lot, the standing house beside it

and sat down
